description: Team Eclipse is a Peru-based, multidisciplinary team blending engineering and 3D (Three.js/React), NASA data research (NSSDCA, mission reports, 3D Resources), narrative design (FACT vs. VOICE) and accessible bilingual UX to tell the stories of abandoned lunar and Martian hardware. Interests: space history, 3D visualization, edutainment, open data, accessibility. Looking for: 3D artists, writers, educators, audio designers, data scientists, accessibility testers and translators.
summary: We are Team Eclipse, and we tell the stories of the machines NASA left behind. From rovers that finished their last command to probes still drifting into deep space, we believe abandoned hardware is not forgotten — it's waiting to be remembered. Blending 3D visualization, data, and narrative, we bring the Moon and Mars relics to life for young space enthusiasts who will one day build what comes next.
details:
What it does / how it works

Astro Archive is a bilingual (EN/ES) web experience made of two companion apps that tell the stories of NASA's abandoned hardware on the Moon, Mars and deep space, for 10–14-year-olds and casual space fans.

1. Astro Archive — 3D Solar System Simulator (astroarchive.earth/astro-archive): a WebGL simulator with real Keplerian orbits (Sun→Pluto, Moon, ISS in LEO). Users pilot a craft, lock onto relics — Apollo 11 Lunar Descent Stage, Ingenuity, Opportunity, Perseverance, Voyager 1 & 2 — and inspect authentic telemetry (power, temperature, signal delay) while listening to digitized Apollo Mission Control audio.

2. Still Listening (astroarchive.earth): a scroll-driven orbital museum of four low-poly dioramas (Eagle, Opportunity, Ingenuity, Dawn). Each artifact has four beats — What it is, Why it went, What it found, What it is now — a labeled fictionalized "voice", and a signal meter (active → dormant → silent → lost). "The Last Interview" RPG gives 4 signal units across 7 questions; what you skip is lost and feeds a persistent Memory Catalog. Two 20-second mini-games teach real constraints: lunar descent (18,184 lb propellant, 770 lb remaining, 1.62 m/s²) and Opportunity's last winter (468 → 22 Wh in the 2018 storm).

Why it matters

We turn discarded equipment into monuments. Every claim is sourced (NSSDCA, NASA Science, Apollo Mission Reports, Apollo Lunar Surface Journal), and the FACT vs. VOICE split lets educators trust the data while the story moves the audience. Fully bilingual EN/ES, with screen-reader-friendly DOM, reduced-motion support, a no-WebGL reading mode and keyboard navigation.

Impact

Inspire the next generation by showing that every abandoned rover and probe still has a story — and a legacy still in use (Apollo 11's retroreflector is still pinged by lasers today).

Tools

JavaScript/TypeScript, React 18/19, Three.js + React Three Fiber (drei, postprocessing), Tailwind CSS, Vite, GLSL shaders, Web Audio API, localStorage; NASA 3D Resources GLB models, NASA/JPL and Solar System Scope textures, images.nasa.gov, digitized Apollo audio. No backend — static deploy.

Creativity

FACT vs. VOICE narrative design; games as pedagogy (an unwinnable energy game recreates Opportunity's final sols); signal-as-emotion; procedural terrain (11,520 triangles, no seams), instanced rocks in one draw call, a dithered sky shader and a normalized model pipeline.

Factors considered

Scientific accuracy and myth-busting (Opportunity's "my battery is low" was a human paraphrase, not a transmission; Ingenuity didn't crash; Dawn still orbits Ceres; only Apollo 11's descent stage is on the Moon); age-appropriateness without oversimplification; performance (~12k triangles, ~390 KB gzip JS); accessibility; NASA attribution without endorsement; scope discipline (Surveyor 3 dropped for lack of an official model).
